title: Who Is the One Who Knows?
reflection: Once today, when you notice a feeling, ask: who is aware of this? Try to point to the one who knows, and see what happens.

questions.q: What is the hidden grammar of all experience, in Conversation 1.2?
o: Every act of knowing has two poles, a knower and a known, joined by the act of knowing.
Every experience has three parts, a past, a present and a future, linked in a chain.
Every experience has one pole only, the known, since the knower is just another object.
Every act of knowing has four stages, from sensing to thinking, in a fixed order.
questions.e: Someone knowing something. The traditions call the known grāhya, what is grasped, and the knower grāhaka, the one who grasps.
questions.c: Knower, known and the act of knowing

questions.q: A woman tries to point to the one who is aware of the cup, the sound and the worry, and finds nothing to grab. What does Conversation 1.2 say?
o: The known is easy to find and the knower is elusive: there is no object to point to.
She has failed, so she should try again with more effort until she finds an object.
She has proved that there is no one aware, since nothing was found when she looked.
She has found the answer, since not finding anything is the same as an empty mind.
questions.e: You can point to the cup, the sound and the worry. When you try to point to the you who is aware of them, there is nothing to grab. This is an observation and not a belief.
questions.c: The knower is elusive, not absent

questions.q: A man notices “I am tired.” What has become an object in that moment, according to Conversation 1.2?
o: The everyday I: whatever can be known is not, finally, the knower.
The Self: the deepest awareness, which has now been caught and can be examined.
The tiredness only: the I stays the knower, since it is never able to be observed.
Nothing: the noticing leaves everything as it was, with no difference of any kind.
questions.e: The moment you notice I am tired, the I in it becomes something you are aware of. And whatever can be known is not, finally, the knower.
questions.c: The everyday I can itself be observed

questions.q: “Like the eye that sees the room but cannot see itself, the knowing cannot be made into an object.”
questions.e: Try to catch the one who knows and you either chase an endless chain or see directly that the knowing is what is doing the looking, like the knife that cannot cut itself.
questions.c: The knowing cannot be made into an object

questions.q: “Conversation 1.2 teaches that the everyday person is not real and that nothing exists but awareness.”
questions.e: This is an observation, not a mystical claim. You still exist; the everyday person is entirely real. Nothing is denied; something is simply seen.
questions.c: Nothing is denied: something is seen

questions.q: What is the difference between self and Self, in Conversation 1.2?
o: The small self is the everyday named person; the capital Self is the awareness it appears in.
The small self is the body and the capital Self is the mind, and the two together make up a whole person.
The small self is a bad part of us and the capital Self is a good part, and the good part should win out.
The small self is the first half of a life and the capital Self is the second half of that same life.
questions.e: Self is not a better version of the small self: it is a different category. One is observed, the other is the observing. Its terms are Ātman and Cit.
questions.c: The small self is observed; the Self is the observing

questions.q: A man thinks, “I am anxious,” and feels that it is the whole truth about him. What does Conversation 1.2 offer?
o: Notice the everyday I inside a wider awareness: the anxiety becomes one event in a larger field.
Treat the anxiety as the whole of himself, since that is the only honest way to meet it at full size.
Forget the anxiety quickly, since noticing it is only a way of making it grow stronger within him.
Describe the anxiety to other people at once, since it is the telling itself that is the whole remedy.
questions.e: If the everyday I is all you are, suffering becomes total. The instant you notice the I inside a wider awareness, space opens around the suffering: one event in a larger field, not the entire sky.

questions.q: A patient says, “I am a failure.” Which reframing from Conversation 1.2 fits mindfulness-based therapy?
o: I am having the thought that I am a failure: a new relationship to the thought.
I am not a failure, since a failure is something that nobody at all could ever be, and so I am not one.
I must stop thinking at once, since thoughts of this kind are the very cause of the failure itself.
I should say it louder, since saying a thought out loud is the best way to make it smaller in me.
questions.e: The heart of mental health is not eliminating difficult experiences but changing your relationship to them, which needs space between the experience and the one who has it.
questions.c: I am having the thought that I am a failure

questions.q: Why does Conversation 1.2 say brain activity is not the same as lived awareness?
o: Knowing which neurons fire in joy describes the machinery, not the joy as lived.
Brain activity is unrelated to experience, so the study of the brain has nothing to teach.
Brain activity is the whole of awareness, so nothing more needs to be said about experience.
Brain activity is only imagined, so that no measurement of it can be trusted by anyone.
questions.e: Keeping the two distinct protects both science and contemplation.
questions.c: Machinery is not the joy as lived

questions.q: A teacher wants to try the practical experiment of Conversation 1.2 this week. What does it ask?
o: Notice a feeling, ask who is aware of it, and look for the one who knows without forcing an answer.
Argue with each feeling, until a clear answer has been found for what it is made of.
Avoid all feelings, so that nothing is left for the one who knows to be aware of.
Write down every feeling of the day, so that a full list can be made at the end of it.
questions.e: The experiment is a looking and not a belief: notice, ask who is aware, and see directly.
questions.c: Look for the knower without forcing an answer
